thread:
maria_sales: BetaCorp POC failing with 413 when they POST conversation + 2 attachments inlined as base64 (~52MB). They can't use presigned URLs due to data residency rules. Need quick triage and pricing guidance.

ben_se: Do we have their raw response / headers? 413 from which hop?

maria_sales: Customer pasted: ```
POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 52348211
< HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
< X-Correlation-ID: betacorp-42
< Server: Microsoft-Azure-ApplicationGateway/v2
```

tia_infra: Azure App Gateway or their fronting NGinx will drop it most likely. If AGW returns 413 it often never reaches our backend. We need ingress trace for the correlation id.

ben_se: If they can't presign, suggest these options: gzip request (Content-Encoding: gzip), split payload into multiple requests with context windowing + pointers, or send attachments to a customer-controlled object store and put secure pointers in the payload.

maria_sales: BetaCorp says compliance forbids external object stores and they need full fidelity of attachments in call. Any product path short-term?

alex_platform: Two product paths: 1) Dedicated with custom ingress - we can accept larger bodies and control proxy settings. 2) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where they run the runtime in their network. Both are onboarding-heavy.

maria_sales: Pricing question from them: will Dedicated increase per-token costs or just a fixed seat/reserved capacity fee? They want a ballpark today.

alex_platform: Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing (monthly or annual commit) + platform fee; per-token inference pricing shouldn't increase by default for identical model configs, but dedicated has minimums and provisioning lead time. For Private there is a platform license and infra costs. I can ping Sales Ops for a non-binding estimate.

tia_infra: Short-term engineering mitigations we can try while pricing is sorted:
- Ask them to try gzip first (often 60-80% reduction).
- Use incremental windowing: only send last N messages + an index of attachments; server-side we can accept a second request to fetch attachments if we set up a temporary transfer (needs agreement).
- Chunked transfer (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) sometimes bypasses Content-Length limits, but many AGW/WAF setups reject chunked.
- For reproducibility: run `curl -v --data-binary @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat` from their network and capture tcpdump/ingress logs.

ben_se: If you want immediate support, we can schedule a 1-hour pairing session with BetaCorp infra team to reproduce from their egress and show the AGW response. That usually resolves policy mismatches quickly.

maria_sales: Please book that pairing. I'll also ask them to try gzipping and to confirm if they can do multipart/form-data without presigned objects.

support-bot: Note: recent platform deploy changed nginx client_max_body_size for some tenants yesterday. Check Console -> Tenant Overrides for `nginx.client_max_body_size`.

tia_infra: Also check any WAF rules for JSON size inspection; sometimes ModSecurity rules cause 413 even when proxy limit is fine.

maria_sales: Booking pairing for tomorrow 10am PT. I'll update BetaCorp that Dedicated is an option but has procurement lead time; meanwhile try gzip and we'll attempt a live repro with them.

ben_se: Added a short doc link for engineering: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbook/large-payloads (contains curl repro, header checklist, and quick examples of splitting context).

maria_sales: Thanks team 609. Marking high priority for the deal.
